title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
statement:
You are given an unordered list of integers and a positive integer k. Your task is to determine the value that would occupy the k-th position if the list were sorted from largest to smallest, without necessarily requiring you to fully sort the entire list.

To be precise: rank all the numbers from the largest value down to the smallest, allowing duplicate values to occupy separate consecutive ranks (i.e., duplicates are not merged into a single rank, if the same number appears multiple times, each occurrence counts as its own position in the ranking). Return the number sitting at rank k in this descending ranking.

While sorting the array and reading off the k-th entry trivially solves the problem, aim for an approach that avoids the full O(n log n) sorting cost when possible, for example, using a heap-based selection strategy or a partition-based (quickselect-style) selection strategy.

examples.explanation: Sorted in descending order the list reads [9, 7, 6, 4, 2, 2]. The 3rd entry in that ordering is 6.
Sorted in descending order the list reads [5, 5, 5, 1]. Since duplicates each occupy their own rank, the 2nd entry is still 5 (the second copy of 5), not the next distinct value.
